recent_posts.title: Enhancing Web Design: Recognizing Accessibility Issues Now
recent_posts.summary: Accessibility is often neglected not because designers are careless, but because there's simply too much to remember. Drawing on Jakob Nielsen's heuristic of 'recognition rather than recall', the author proposes using accessibility personas (from the book 'A Web for Everyone') as a practical design tool. Eight personas representing users with various disabilities and needs are introduced, each with real-world quotes that highlight specific design pain points. The recommended workflow involves assigning a 'Designated Dissenter' on each project team to ask how each persona would experience the design, then consulting platform-specific accessibility guidelines (WCAG 2.2, Material Design, Apple, Windows, Ubuntu) to address identified issues.

recent_posts.title: Designing Amiable Web Spaces: Lessons from Vienna's Café Culture
recent_posts.summary: Drawing from Vienna's café culture and the Vienna Circle's collaborative research environment (1928-1934), this piece explores design principles for fostering amiable online interactions. Eight key factors promoted productive disagreement: seriousness of purpose, empiricism, abstraction, formality, self-deprecating humor, openness, parody as social correction, and appropriate engagement levels. The café's physical design—customizable service, neutral third space, permeable boundaries—combined with human moderation from multiple voices created an environment where diverse, difficult personalities could disagree productively. These historical lessons offer frameworks for designing web spaces that encourage constructive discourse rather than conflict, particularly relevant for support forums, news sites, and community platforms.

recent_posts.title: Embracing Design Dialects: Enhancing User Experience
recent_posts.summary: Design systems should function like living languages that can develop contextual dialects while maintaining core principles. Rather than enforcing rigid consistency, successful design systems allow systematic adaptations for specific user contexts and constraints. Examples from Booking.com, Shopify, and Atlassian demonstrate how flexible frameworks enable teams to modify components based on user needs while preserving brand unity. The key is balancing consistency with fluency, prioritizing user task completion over aesthetic uniformity.

recent_posts.title: An Holistic Framework for Shared Design Leadership
recent_posts.summary: A framework for effective collaboration between Design Managers and Lead Designers using a biological organism metaphor. The approach divides team health into three systems: nervous (people & psychology, managed primarily by Design Manager), muscular (craft & execution, led by Lead Designer), and circulatory (strategy & flow, shared responsibility). Rather than creating territorial divisions, both roles work together as caretakers of different aspects of the same healthy design team, with clear primary responsibilities but overlapping support roles.

recent_posts.title: From Beta to Bedrock: Build Products that Stick.
recent_posts.summary: Building successful financial products involves avoiding the pitfalls of feature-first development and focusing on core user needs. Embracing the Minimum Viable Product (MVP) approach ensures that products are simple, maintainable, and valuable. Concentrating on 'bedrock' elements—those core functions that truly matter to users—provides long-term stability and value. Strategies include having a clear mission, prioritizing simplicity, continuous iteration, and thorough user testing.

recent_posts.title: User Research Is Storytelling
recent_posts.summary: User research is storytelling. It follows a three-act structure similar to movies: setup, conflict, and resolution. Each act corresponds to a part of the research process: foundational research, directional research, and resolving the identified problems. User research is crucial for understanding users, identifying problems, and creating user-centered designs. It helps stakeholders make informed decisions and improve the product.

recent_posts.title: To Ignite a Personalization Practice, Run this Prepersonalization Workshop
recent_posts.summary: The post discusses the importance of prepersonalization workshops for successful personalization practices, using examples from Spotify and other organizations. It emphasizes the need for effective collaboration and planning, and provides a framework for conducting such workshops.

recent_posts.title: The Wax and the Wane of the Web
recent_posts.summary: The post discusses the evolution of web design and development, from the early days of using tables and limited typefaces to the current era of modern web applications. It highlights the importance of building for the long haul, starting from standards, designing with care, always learning, playing and experimenting, and sharing and amplifying. The post encourages readers to embrace change and contribute to making the web a better place.

recent_posts.title: Opportunities for AI in Accessibility
recent_posts.summary: This post explores the potential uses of AI in improving accessibility for people with disabilities. It discusses the challenges and opportunities in areas such as generating alternative text for images, matching algorithms for job seekers, voice preservation and recognition, text transformation, and the importance of diverse teams and data.

recent_posts.title: I am a creative.
